rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords may raise rent only once a year by no more than the lesser of 3% or 80% of the CPI change. Landlords may charge a pass-through fee of up to $50 per rental unit, and tenants may petition for review of excess increases.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change; 2.87% for 1 Sep 2026 to 31 Aug 2027
rules.penalty: Landlord must reimburse a tenant charged a registration fee pass-through above $50.
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.status_basis: City page describes the ordinance as in force and announces the current maximum increase.
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a valid reason to evict, such as nonpayment, lease violation, or owner move-in. Landlords may have to pay relocation assistance for certain no-fault evictions.
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.status_basis: City page describes the ordinance as in force.
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
